[WILL NOT FIX: superseded by OGC-1383] Microbiology admin: culture setup form has no reportable analyte field
fields.description:
**Found while diagnosing OGC-1384** on https://amr.openelis-global.org.

## What happens

`GET /rest/microbiology/admin/reference/culture-setups` on the AMR server:

* "Bacteriology" (method 53, Plate Culturing): **no** `reportableTestAnalyteId`
* "UAT bacteriology culture" (52) and "UAT alternate bacteriology culture" (54): have one (e.g. 294). These came from the UAT scenario seeding, not the admin screen.

Every case made under a setup without a reportable analyte has `mappingConfigured: false` and can never be final-released (OGC-1384).

## Cause

* The culture setup form definition (`frontend/src/components/admin/microbiologyReference/definitions.js`) offers method, name, workflow, media, incubation, subculture, max days, atmosphere and active, but **not the reportable test analyte**. The API accepts `reportableTestAnalyteId` (`MicroCultureSetupAdminForm`), and only the configuration loader and the UAT scenario set it.
* **Likely, not yet confirmed:** `saveCultureSetup` sets `reportableTestAnalyteId` from the request with `trimToNull`, so saving an existing setup from the admin form (which does not send the field) may clear it. Editing the UAT setups in the UI could break their release too.

## Expected

1. The culture setup form lets an admin choose the reportable test and analyte. Pick from reportable analytes of the test, and check that the test has an active REMARK result type, or explain why it can't be used.
2. Saving the form never clears a field the form does not show.
3. The setup list shows which setups are not ready to release reports.

fields.summary: [WILL NOT FIX: superseded by OGC-1383] Microbiology: "Final release ready" but Release final report stays disabled (patient-report mapping missing)
fields.description:
**Found by:** Casey, on https://amr.openelis-global.org, case 26PHML00003L (`b7c94607-2ec0-49a2-a3cd-f9f3c11c277f`, Urines, Bacteriology, stage PRELIM_RELEASED). Verified with the case's own REST responses.

## What happens

The workflow is complete and the Reports section shows **"Final release ready ✓"** with no blockers, but **Release final report** is disabled. Nothing on the page says why, except a small grey tag under the preview: "Patient-report mapping required for final release".

## What the server returns for this case

* `GET /rest/microbiology/cases/{id}/readiness` → `finalReleaseReady: true`, `blockers: []`
* `GET /rest/microbiology/cases/{id}/release/preview` → `reportableContent: true`, `mappingConfigured: false`, `projectedResultIds: []`

## Cause

* `ReportReadinessPanel.jsx` enables the button only when `readiness.finalReleaseReady && projection.reportableContent && projection.mappingConfigured`. The readiness service (`MicroCaseReadinessServiceImpl`) never checks the mapping, so it can report "ready" while the button stays off.
* `mappingConfigured` (`MicroReportProjectionServiceImpl.hasReportConfiguration`) needs every `micro_case_analysis` link to have a `reportable_test_analyte_id`, and the test must have an active REMARK test result.
* The link copies `reportable_test_analyte_id` from the culture setup **when the case is created** (`MicroCaseAnalysisServiceImpl.linkAnalysis`). This case used culture setup "Bacteriology" (method 53, Plate Culturing), which has no reportable analyte. The two UAT setups (methods 52 and 54) have one, which is why UAT cases release.
* Fixing the setup later does not repair existing cases: `linkAnalysis` returns the existing link unchanged.

## Expected

1. Readiness reports the mapping (and reportable content) as blockers, with plain wording and the test or setup to fix. "Final release ready" is never shown while release is impossible.
2. Existing cases pick up a corrected culture setup mapping (re-resolve at preview/release, or backfill), so a stuck case can be released without database work.
3. Case 26PHML00003L can be final-released once the setup is fixed.

## Related

Culture setup admin has no way to set the reportable analyte: see the linked ticket.

Basic Info — AMR flag + conditional WHONET fields + retention behavior
fields.description:
## Summary

AMR test flag checkbox that, when enabled, reveals the WHONET configuration sub-form. AMR disable retention behavior: historical exports unchanged; new results respect the flag; WHONET config persists.

**Parent epic:** OGC-748
**FRS:** §2.1, v2.4 §AMR Test Flag, H-04

## Acceptance criteria

* \[ \] Carbon `<Checkbox>` "Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) Test" with helper text "Enable for WHONET export and antimicrobial resistance surveillance"
* \[ \] When checked, conditional sub-section reveals:

    * WHONET Antibiotic Code: typeahead Carbon `<ComboBox>` populated from `whonet_antibiotic_codes` reference table
    * Antibiotic Class: Carbon `<Select>` (Penicillins / Fluoroquinolones / Cephalosporins / etc.)
    * Test Method: Carbon `<Select>` (Disk Diffusion / MIC / E-test)
    * Breakpoint Standard: Carbon `<Select>` (CLSI 2024 / EUCAST 2024 / Custom)
    * Disk Potency: Carbon `<NumberInput>` with µg suffix
    
* \[ \] Info banner when AMR is enabled: "This test will be included in WHONET exports"
* \[ \] Persists to `test.is_amr_test` and `test_amr_config`
* \[ \] **AMR retention (H-04):** when admin disables AMR on a test that already has results:

    * Historical results retain their result-time export status (already-exported stays exported)
    * Results queued for export still go out
    * New results created while AMR is OFF are not eligible for export
    * WHONET config persists on the test record so re-enabling restores the full config in one click
    
* \[ \] All visible strings i18n-wrapped

## Estimated size

M (\~2 days)

fields.description:
## Overview

Unifies what was previously split between AMR Configuration §9 (Hub for organism/antibiotic/AST Panel updates) and WHONET Integration §2.3 (Import Hub for WHONET codes). One admin page, one mechanism, four data domains.

The Hub is a central repository (managed externally by an OE community / consortium) that supplies updates to reference data: breakpoint tables, organism master entries, antibiotic master entries, and WHONET code mappings. OE pulls; never pushes.

## Scope

**Phase 1B** — depends on M-01, M-02, M-09 having something to update.

* `hub_subscription_config` (singleton) + `hub_import_run` + `hub_import_record` audit schemas
* Hub Subscription config page (URL, encrypted API key, subscribed domains, auto-check frequency)
* Test Connection action
* Auto-check scheduler (Daily / Weekly / Monthly)
* Available Updates page (per-domain summary)
* Preview Changes side panel (diff: Added / Updated / Locally Customized)
* Import action per domain (Merge / Replace seeded / Replace all)
* Locally customized row protection (skip rows with `locally_customized = true`)
* Import History page

## Source documents

* `m-10-hub-subscription-frs-v1.md`

## Sizing

\~32 story points across 12 sub-stories.

## Consumers

* M-01 AMR Reference Data — organism / antibiotic / AST Panel updates
* M-02 Breakpoint Catalog — breakpoint standard updates (new versions land as Loaded, not Active; lab manager activates explicitly per M-02 §8)
* M-09 WHONET Export — WHONET code mapping updates

## Verification dependencies

* Hub URL endpoint format and API contract (managed externally — verify with Hub maintainer team)
* Encrypted API key storage path in OE

## Supersedes

OGC-293 (in part) — closed as superseded. This is one of 14 epics in the M-\* bundle.
